div.head: I Cn 22.2
div.ab: Crist sylf sang Pater noster ærest ⁊ þæt gebed his leorningcnihtum tæhte.
Crist sylf sang Pater noster ærest ⁊ þæt gebed his leorni[n]gcnihtum teahte.
Crist seolf sangc Pater noster arost ⁊ þæt gebedd his leorningcnihtum tæhte.
Christus ipse primus hanc orationem protulit et discipulos suos docuit.
[22, 2] Christus ipse ‘Pater noster’ prius cantauit et postea discipulos suos docuit.
Ipse enim dominus Ihesus Christus primus illam oracionem orauit suisque discipulis insinuauit.
Crist sylf sang Pater noster ærest ⁊ þæt gebed his leorni[n]gcnihtum teahte.
Crist sylf sang Pater noster ærest and þæt gebed his leorningccnihtum tæhte.
Christus selbst zuerst sang Pater noster und lehrte dies Gebet seinen Jüngern.
Christ himself first sang the Pater noster and taught that prayer to his disciples.
Christ himself first recited the Pater Noster and taught the prayer to his disciples.
Christ himself first recited the Paternoster and taught that prayer to his disciples.
div.note: Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 303, October 2026 (MS Cons)

note.seg: pr. ‘P. n.’ Cb T; pr. c. ‘P. n.’ Lb S
pr. ‘P. n.’ Cb T; pr. c. ‘P. n.’ Lb S

‘liturgisch hersagen’ ist, laut 22, 3, mitgemeint; auch die Lateiner verstehen ‘singen’ nicht zu eng. Aber im Altfranz. Epos ‘Reise Karls’ betritt Karl d. Gr. in Jerusalem eine Kirche, wo Gott selbst die Messe sang mit den 12 Aposteln; Suchier Französ. Lit. Geschi. 27. Wulfstan 20f. lässt hier das (wegen o. 22) zum Zusammenhang Nötige folgen: leorningcnihtas . . sungon Crede

‘Recite liturgically’ is, according to 22, 3, also meant; the Latin translators, too, do not understand ‘sing’ too narrowly. But in the Old French epic ‘Voyage of Charlemagne’ Charlemagne enters a church in Jerusalem where God himself sang mass with the 12 apostles; Suchier Französ. Lit. Geschi. 27. Wulfstan 20f. here goes on with what the context requires (because of above 22): leorningcnihtas . . sungon Crede
